reason: This passage (1 Chronicles 21) describes David taking a census of Israel, which incurs God's displeasure and results in a plague. Critically, when the people suffer greatly, David explicitly takes personal responsibility for the sin, stating 'I have sinned greatly' (וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִים חָטָאתִֽי מְאֹ֔ד) and 'I am the one who sinned' (וַאֲנִי־ הוּא אֲשֶׁר־ חָטָאתִי). More tellingly, David explicitly exonerates the people, saying 'these [people] - what have they done?' (וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַצֹּ֖אן מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ), indicating they are innocent victims. The text demonstrates the opposite of the statement: a leader accepting blame and defending the people rather than blaming them for suffering caused by his own action.
